objective: Retire the two named census residuals rather than harden a twice-falsified design a third time. The admission census judges the daemon's source; its own assertion text said it is not rustc's file set and does not claim to be, because a mod walk has no totality edge. Entailment turned out to be reachable from the cheapest possible layer: rustc already writes the exact list of files it read, per binary, as dep-info.
falsifiable_claim: Every .rs file rustc read under the daemon binary's tree is a module the census walked, and every module the census walked is a file rustc read — both directions, against dep-info regenerated by a build in the same run so the entailed set describes this tree. The non-Rust files rustc read are matched by name against the census's own PRODUCTION include records, so an unexplained file is a finding whatever its extension. The unadjudicable bucket vocabulary is closed in both directions: every bucket the resolver's own source can emit is pinned, every pinned bucket is one it can emit, and ambiguous-module, not-a-visible-const and resolution-cycle are each pinned at zero. The census's own count pins and mutation battery are composed rather than restated.

code_anchors.literal: RESIDUAL 1 — every Rust file the COMPILER read
the unadjudicable bucket VOCABULARY is closed

adversarial_or_fault_proof: Five drills, each aimed at one finding: a file the compiler read that the census did not walk (the exact shape of the redirect and macro-mod constructs the census said it could not see), a module the compiler never read, a bucket the resolver can emit that no pin mentions, a pin whose code path no longer exists, and a non-Rust file rustc read that the census does not record. The run also corrected its own first construction: run 1 compared ALL 93 recorded includes against the binary's dep-info and went red on four #[cfg(test)] fixtures rustc had no reason to read — a true difference between two sets that are not the same subject. The comparison is now restricted to production includes, which is what a binary's dep-info can speak to.
remaining_nonclaims: Entailment is per BINARY. This proves the daemon binary's file set; the test harness compiles a different set, and this check says nothing about it.

The bucket vocabulary is derived from the resolver's own source by matching its `bucket:` literals. A resolver that emitted a bucket name through a computed string rather than a literal would not appear, and that construct does not exist in this resolver today.
The census's counts remain the census's own claim. This unit adds the two residuals and composes that gate; it does not re-derive or re-litigate its pins.
source_provenance: Landed 2026-09-12 by the MVP finish-line program, leg 2 (first unit of the READY set). Measured: rustc reads 118 files under crates/node/src/bin/ for the daemon binary — 116 Rust modules, matching the census exactly in both directions, plus 2 JSON data includes the census records by name as include_str! arguments it pins rather than follows. check:admission-census-entailment 7/7 with the census composed; mutate: 12/12 with all five drills catching their planted defects.
